text:
tiffany: FYI I'm seeing a big spike in pending pods for gpu-pool-us-central, queueing requests and causing tail latency to jump ~3x. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/regions/us-central/pools/gpu-pool-us-central

maya: thanks — checking the autoscaler logs now. initial glance: scale controller getting noisy metrics, repeatedly adding and removing 4-8 nodes in 10m window. looks like a feedback loop.

autoscale-bot: [alert] scale-controller: high-provisioning-latency detected (avg 48s) for gpu-pool-us-central, provisioning-failures=12, recent-fallbacks=3

alex: provisioning is slow because GCP quota hits for NVIDIA T4s in that region. we have capacity but quota bump pending from cloud. I've opened ticket with provider (INC-4321). ETA unknown.

raj: got it. In the meantime traffic is still targeted to us-central. I propose we temporarily shift new requests to eu-west with lower GPU queue, and drain non-critical workloads from us-central so provisioning pressure drops.

maya: agree. two problems: 1) autoscaler is thrashing on noisy `pending_pods` metric (we're reacting to transient backlog spikes) 2) the controller's cool-down and max-scale-step settings are too aggressive for bursty chat workloads.

tiffany: can we mute the scale controller's reactive rule and set a minimum stable replicas until quotas clear?

alex: yes. I can patch controller config: set stabilizationWindowSeconds=120, maxSurge=2, and set metric-policy: require 2 consecutive windows over threshold. planning to apply now.

maya: also adding a rate-limiter on autoscale decisions: `--max-scale-ops-per-minute=2` so it won't oscillate.

maya: command I'm running on the controller: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/scale-controller -- /bin/scalectl apply --pool gpu-pool-us-central --stabilization 120s --max-ops 2`

deploy-bot: deploy started by alex: scale-controller-config-v2026-03-18-1. rolling update to 3/3 pods

tiffany: switching routing: I'm going to add eu-west fallback in the routing policy and mark us-central as degraded. Will keep a 20% traffic cap to eu-west for gradual shift.

raj: note: eu-west latency for some customers increases ~50–80ms, but it's better than request timeouts. Also embeddings jobs might see different model variants, set `model_priority: [redwood-3b-quant, redwood-3b]` for eu-west to maintain cost parity.

maya: patch took effect — scale-controller stopped flapping. provisioning failures remain but are no longer causing oscillation. pending_pods peaked at ~420 -> now stable ~90.

autoscale-bot: [info] autoscaler: stabilization active for gpu-pool-us-central (120s). suppressing scale-downs.

alex: cloud ticket updated: provider acknowledges quota bottleneck, but manual region failover requires approval for cross-region burst credits. Security ok for eu-west routing but we need to sign off on data residency for 3 customers. cc: legal/sales.

tiffany: noted. I've added exception for sessions labeled `tier=selfhost` to stick to us-central. We'll only shift public/free-tier requests.

raj: quick mitigation: I disabled prefix-KV caching for chat-lite workloads in us-central to reduce per-request memory pressure (config change: `cache.prefix_enabled=false` for chat-lite). That dropped memory usage per replica ~7%.

maya: good call. also rebalanced some ephemeral jobs to our dedicated reserved pool in us-west to reduce burst pressure on shared pool.

alex: cost note: shifting ~25% of traffic to eu-west increases immediate egress/cross-region costs. forecasting ~+$3k/day if this stays for >48h. prefer to keep until quota bump done or we open temporary reserved nodes in us-central.

tiffany: agree prefer quota bump. For now keep routing cap at 30% and monitor error budget. status update in 30m.

maya: follow-ups: 1) tweak autoscaler metrics to use smoothed pending_pods (5m EWMA) instead of raw 1m spikes 2) add provision-failure retry threshold bump to 5 before fallback 3) run a load replay test to validate stabilizationWindow 4) postmortem if quota issue >24h.

alex: I'll provision a small reserved burst pool (2x T4) in us-central as stopgap if provider can't act within 6 hours. need billing approval.

tiffany: thumbs up. can someone add a short incident note to incidents/ with timeline and actions?

maya: adding initial incident note Draft: "Pulse spike caused rapid pending_pods increase in gpu-pool-us-central. Autoscaler reacted to noisy signals and entered a thrash loop while cloud GPU quota constrained provisioning. Mitigations: stabilization window, autoscale rate-limit, temporary routing to eu-west (30%), cache and job rebalancing, reserved burst pool request. Next: metric smoothing, repro test, provider quota follow-up."

raj: repro test plan posted: https://playbooks.redwood/repro/pulse-spike-2026-03-18 — includes script to simulate 1k concurrent chat sessions.

autoscale-bot: [resolved] alert cleared for scale-controller thrash.

tiffany: thanks all. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to SEs if quota ETA slips. :eyes:

maya: final note — let's schedule a 30m retro tomorrow to lock down autoscaler defaults for bursty workloads.

alex: copying legal + billing about cross-region exception.

tiffany: end of thread for now.
